findings.claim: In contractless mode, `CreateContractlessMembers` selects every public read-write member and never looks at member attributes. A type with no `[MessagePackObject]` or `[DataContract]` therefore still has members marked `[IgnoreMember]` serialized. The same is true for `[IgnoreDataMember]`, which a zero-dependency Project A can use because it is in the BCL. This breaks the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured. The existing contractless resolver skips such members, so a member the type author excluded (for example a secret) is written to the wire.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.cs::ContractlessMode_HonoursIgnoreMember. It drives CSharpGeneratorDriver over a contractless MyObject that has `[IgnoreMember] public int SecretValue`, then asserts the generated formatter does not reference SecretValue. On head it does.

findings.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration. A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F` nested inside a NON-partial containing class passes every check, and no diagnostic is reported. The emitted code (via EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and the qualified formatter name) then either redeclares the container as partial, which gives CS0260, or emits F outside it, which gives CS0535 on the user's class. Either way the user gets a raw compiler error instead of MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.cs::NestedFormatterInNonPartialContainer_ReportsDiagnosticOrCompiles. It asserts that either the generator reports an error diagnostic or the post-generation compilation has no errors. On head neither holds.

findings.claim: The model built for a user-declared formatter is added to `modelPerType` with no check for whether T is also collected by the TypeCollector. Example: T is in the same compilation and carries `[MessagePackObject]`. Then the resolver gets two ObjectInfos for the same DataType, the auto-generated `internal sealed` formatter and the user's partial one. This causes duplicate registration or hint-name collisions, or the sorted-set merge silently drops one of them, which leaves the user's partial class unimplemented.

receipt_plan.detail: Read MessagePackGenerator.cs:68-74 next to the existing Collect(typeSymbol) loop: nothing deduplicates by DataType. Confirm with a generator test where a `[MessagePackObject]` T and a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` formatter for that T coexist, plus a `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]`, and check for CS8785/CS0535 or a duplicate resolver case.
